S&P 500 · ESG + Financial + Image AI

Reading investment risk
in the shape of a stock.

A hybrid classifier that fuses environmental, social and governance data with a year of price history — encoded as an image — to sort S&P 500 companies into Low, Medium or High risk, and explain every call it makes.

The problem

ESG scores and price risk are usually judged separately. They shouldn't be.

A company's environmental, social and governance profile shapes the risks it's exposed to — regulatory, reputational, physical. Those risks eventually show up in how its stock actually trades. Most tools report one or the other. We built a model that reads both at once: the numbers and the shape of a year of price movement.

Fragmented signal

ESG ratings, financial fundamentals, and price history usually live in separate tools with separate vocabularies.

Black-box risk tools

Many risk scores can't be interrogated — you get a label with no reasoning behind it.

Our approach

Fuse ESG, fundamentals and a visual encoding of price history into one classifier, and explain every prediction with SHAP.

65+ metrics — margins, valuation ratios, cash position — parsed from mixed-format strings (1.2B, 3.5%, Yes/No).

DS4
5-Year Daily Prices
619,040 rows · Name

Open/high/low/close/volume history — the last 252 trading days become each company's price fingerprint.

Leakage control: Total ESG Risk score, overallRisk and ESG percentile are the columns that create the label — they're excluded as features. Component scores, financials and price-derived stats are the valid inputs.

FIG. 02 — PRICE AS AN IMAGE

Turning a year of prices into a fingerprint

A Gramian Angular Summation Field (GASF) re-encodes a 1-D price series as a 2-D image, so a convolutional network can "see" the trend and volatility patterns that a table of numbers hides.

01
Take the trailing window

The last 252 close prices — roughly one trading year — per company.

02
Subsample to 64 points

Evenly spaced samples compress the year to a fixed 64×64 image size.

03
Normalise to [−1, 1]

Min-max scaling makes every company's fingerprint comparable regardless of share price.

x′ = 2(x−min)/(max−min) − 1
04
Encode as angles, then a field

Each value becomes an angle; the field is the cosine of every angle pair — a 64×64 matrix that visually encodes trend and turbulence.

φ = arccos(x′)  ·  GASF[i,j] = cos(φi + φj)

AAPL · 252-day GASF fingerprint

FIG. 02B — ACTUAL PIPELINE OUTPUT

Six of the 364 real GASF images the notebook generated, next to the price series each was built from. Diagonal green streaks mark strong trends; the scattered red/orange of XOM (High risk) shows the turbulence the CNN is meant to pick up on.

FIG. 03 — MODEL ARCHITECTURE

Two ways of seeing a company, fused into one call

Four models were built and compared honestly, including the ones that underperformed. The winner fuses frozen image embeddings with tabular features through a gradient-boosted tree.

Image branch

Frozen ResNet50

Pretrained on ImageNet, never fine-tuned on our labels — ruling out leakage. Each 64×64 GASF image becomes a 2,048-dimension embedding pulled from the res_bn layer.

Tabular branch

ESG + Financial features

Environment / social / governance component scores, beta, market cap, and volatility-adjusted return metrics, imputed and scaled on the training fold only.

2,048-d image embedding + tabular features → XGBoost · Optuna-tuned (25 trials) → Low / Medium / High + SHAP
